trustBoundary.interpretation: SELECTOR OVER A T0-VALIDATED PROJECTION (the ruling preferred interpretation)
selectorEnforcesOnItsOwnAuthority: the evidence reference names the WORK plane
the evidence carries a canonical id
the evidence project scope matches when present
the compared identity field equals the requested attempt
reliesOnT0For: owner reference resolution and verification state
explicitlyNotA: standalone validator of arbitrary externally supplied projections
trustBoundary.whyThisIsCorrect: T0 has already run buildProjectTrajectory over the canonical Work events before the selector sees anything; re-verifying its source resolution here would duplicate T0 and could only produce a divergent second authority

quarantinePrecision.before: deduplicated by relation NAME, so distinct rejected edges of one relation collapsed and later reasons were lost; scope used the broad canonicalEventIds set, which includes the attempt AUTHORIZATION event that two attempts can share
quarantinePrecision.after: entries carry a stable edgeId (trajectoryEdgeIdOf) and are deduplicated by it; scope requires the edge to touch one of the attempt OWN identities (creation, terminal, completed)
measured: two distinct rejected ATTEMPT_PRODUCED_RESULT edges are BOTH reported with distinct edgeIds
a shared authorization node no longer makes another Attempt rejected relation this Attempt quarantined fact
a genuinely rejected edge of this attempt is still reported

verdict: PASS — the trust boundary is explicit and tested; quarantine preserves edge identity and exact Attempt scope
limitations: the selector is not hardened against a deliberately malformed projection; that is T0 responsibility by design and is recorded rather than duplicated
